correctness.rationale: The proof first reduces the weighted constant to the radius profile F(t) by the exact symmetry identity J(lambda)=s F((1-s)/s). For F(t), the affine-regular decagon's dihedral isometries reduce x to half of one edge and y to five edge classes. Writing w=t beta makes every support value affine in (alpha,t,w). For each of the two affine target branches and each ordered pair of norm supports, the possible maximum of the minimum of the two excesses is attained either at a triangular-prism vertex or on the equality plane with two domain facets active. The bundled exact Q(sqrt(5)) certificate exhausts all 1000 edge-interval-support cases and proves every simultaneous support excess nonpositive. Two explicit unit pairs attain the respective bounds for the whole branch intervals, so the supremum formula and transition are exact.
risks: The symmetry reduction relies on the displayed affine-regular decagon and its explicit linear isometries; other decagonal normalizations require conjugating the coordinates.
No claim is made that every maximizing pair is listed.

originality.rationale: The defining 2021 article was inspected in full around its generalized-James section: it introduces J(lambda,X), gives general bounds and structural results, and does not compute the affine-regular decagonal profile. Searches used the exact invariant, the decagon/affine-regular aliases, the radius reparametrization, the endpoint value, and implication-equivalent wording. A same-invariant exact ell_p result, a prior regular-octagon weighted profile, and the known ordinary-decagon endpoint were compared statement-by-statement. None implies the two-branch formula or the extremizer switch away from the midpoint.
residual_risks: Bibliographic and semantic searches cannot establish absolute novelty.
An equivalent formula could exist under another affine normalization or under the radius parameter F(t) rather than lambda.
The ordinary midpoint James value is already known; only the complete weighted profile and branch transition are asserted as new here.
risks: No independent human literature audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The result resolves a continuous one-parameter invariant on a canonical non-Hilbert polyhedral plane, rather than adding a single tabulated number. The golden-ratio threshold marks a genuine change of extremizing configuration, so the profile contains geometric information invisible at the ordinary James midpoint. It also provides a sharp benchmark contrasting with the previously computed single-branch regular-octagon profile and with smooth ell_p formulas.
risks: The value is a model-space benchmark, not a classification theorem for all regular polygons.
